The Story

One forest.
A thousand little surprises.

Barnaby lives where the pines grow tall and the mushrooms glow after rain. He is not a brave moose. He is not a fast moose. He is a curious one — and in these woods, curiosity is the only tool you really need.

Every story begins the same gentle way: something small and strange appears. A humming box in the ferns. A feather that lands on the tip of his enormous nose. A trail of soft light disappearing into a tunnel. Barnaby leans in — nose first, always nose first — and the forest answers.

Nothing here is scary for long. Whatever pops out becomes a friend, a game, or a very silly chase, and every adventure ends the way it started: a warm sweater, quiet trees, and a moose already wondering what is behind the next one.

“If you can't see what's inside, you have to put your nose in.”

— Barnaby's entire life philosophy

The Cast

Meet the cast

One very round moose, one very small ball of light, and a forest that keeps handing them things to worry about.

Series lead

Barnaby

He was knitted into that sweater, as far as anyone can tell — no one has ever seen him without it. He talks less than he sniffs, celebrates absolutely everything, and treats a closed lid as a personal invitation.

Species
Moose. A remarkably round one.
The nose
Enormous, black, glossy. Enters every room before he does.
Antlers
Small. He is still very proud of them.
Signature move
Two hops, then one spin. Performed after any success, however minor.
Favourite sound
The pop of a lid coming loose.
Weakness
Feathers. One landing on his nose ends the whole scene.

Pip

A pocket-sized sunburst with no feet and no fear. Pip floats, glows, and squares up to things a hundred times its size — usually while Barnaby is still deciding whether to look.

Species
A tiny spiked sunburst — half creature, half warm light.
Getting about
No feet at all. Floats, darts and loops through the air.
The glow
Dims to a whisper for hiding — or flares up like a very small sun.
Courage
Wildly out of proportion. Will shout down a mountain troll.
Voice
Squeaky, tiny, and far louder than anyone expects.
Heading for
Home — the Ancient Sun-Tree, somewhere past the dark caves.
Sidekick
See their adventures Colour them in

For grown-ups

What we do — and don't — put in front of your child

Ages 2–6

Written for preschoolers: simple sentences, one idea at a time, no plots to keep track of.

Soft sound

No shrieks, no sudden bangs, no shouting. Surprises are played for giggles, not for fright.

Calm endings

Episodes close on a gentle loop rather than a cliffhanger, so "one more" stays your decision.

Small studio

Made by an independent team in the Niagara region of Ontario, Canada — for Canadian and US families.

Get a note when a new episode drops

One short email per episode. New colouring sheets included. No noise, ever.
